minutes.headline: New Budget Task Force elected a chair, vice chair and clerk, set an hourly biweekly meeting plan and assigned homework.
minutes.summary: At its kickoff meeting the Budget Task Force chose officers, settled on one-hour evening meetings roughly every two weeks through the end of the calendar year, and discussed strategy: comparable towns, demographics, mandated versus discretionary spending, and employee data. Members agreed on homework for next time (comps and town and employee demographics), set the next meeting, and heard one public commenter.

public_comment.topic: A school committee member and Tony's alternate (stated address 21 Francis Ave) suggested starting with a demographics presentation: free and reduced lunch, seniors versus students, roads, home prices, and trends.
A speaker suggested gathering union versus non-union information because salary changes require bargaining, and contract end dates.

Mr. pasos urged the task force not to cut well-run town departments like fire, police and public works, asked for a report of long-term town needs and costs for 2026-2028, and said turnover is partly a workplace issue not only salary.

votes.motion: Elect Tony as chair of the task force
Retract nomination of Evan Waters as vice chair
Nominate Renee as clerk; all in favor

budget_items.what_was_said: The task force's aim was described as looking at money in and out, alternate revenue sources beyond an override, and projecting department and school expenses.

budget_items.topic: Capital planning and municipal building projects
budget_items.what_was_said: Capital planning projects deficits in future years unless funded at requested levels, and the building projects raise tolerance questions.
A member proposed ranking expenses by legal mandate such as special education, versus discretionary items like streets, to show flexibility.

budget_items.topic: Out-of-district placement costs and state rates
budget_items.what_was_said: Out-of-district tuition rates are set by the state and the district cannot protest increases.
A member noted a comparable town has separate residential and commercial tax rates.

decisions.decision: Meeting format by general consensus: roughly one-hour meetings every two weeks, 7 to 8 pm, with occasional two-hour meetings starting earlier; run through end of calendar year; homework-based model with a one-to-two page deliverable.
Charge to be updated on the town website to add the alternate.
Next meeting homework: demographics of the town, comparable towns for school and municipal sides, and employee information.
Members volunteered: school comps by one member; town demographics by another; DESE comps to be used.
Next meeting set for the 22nd at 6 pm to 7 pm in the library with a remote option.

what_happened.line: The new Budget Task Force elected a chair, a vice chair and a clerk, each by a vote that passed with the count not stated.
Members agreed by consensus, with no motion, to meet about an hour every two weeks, 7 to 8 pm, through the end of the calendar year.
The task force set its homework: town demographics, comparable towns for the school and municipal sides, and employee information.
Members discussed ranking expenses as mandated or discretionary, and noted that out-of-district tuition rates are set by the state.
The next meeting was set for the 22nd, 6 to 7 pm, at the library with a remote option.

why_it_matters: The task force is setting up how it will study town and school spending, revenue sources beyond an override, and capital needs, so its early choices shape what residents are later shown.
Its work on mandated versus discretionary costs and on comparable towns could frame any future override or budget question put to voters.
